reflection:
Disciplined no-trade day. Three converging reasons made this an easy hold: (1) already over my 5-position cap with 7 open trades carried from prior sessions, (2) the #1 Super candidate STX is parabolically extended ~70% past its VCP pivot — this is a textbook FOMO trap masquerading as strength, (3) the #2 Super candidate LITE reports earnings tomorrow.

The shadow log warning is significant: 15 would-buys / 0 skips in 5 days. That ratio is wildly out of line with reality — I've been over-trading and rationalizing. Today I followed the rules instead of forcing action. The evidence-backed rule [744aa229] (avoid 'far_from_high' — but more importantly, avoid 'far_from_PIVOT') applies here in spirit: STX at 0.0% from 52w high after a +7.91% gap is not a low-risk entry, it's an 'in-the-blow-off' entry.

Book is healthy: MU +10.5%, FIX +7.2%, VRT +6.6% leading; only GEV slightly underwater at -2.4%, well within stop. Earnings sweep on existing positions confirmed all clear for 7+ days — the 4/29 process rule is now habit.

Key lesson reinforced: when the screener's top names are either (a) extended 50%+ past pivot or (b) reporting tomorrow, the correct action is zero. The screener finds what's strong; the operator decides what's actionable. Most days, the intersection is small.
